note: Delaware County Conservation's 239-acre park and wildlife area 2 mi NE of Greeley along the Elk Creek (Fountain Springs) trout stream, in a narrow wooded valley reached by gravel Oak Road; primitive camping only. The county warns the valley floods in heavy rain. --Claude
summary: Free camping NOT supported: no page says free and the county's camping rules say 'Fees Required', so $0 cleared (rate unknown). Confirmed primitive (no hookups), vault toilets, FCFS no reservations, 14 of 19 days. Season year_round -> false (vehicle access closed late fall/winter). Pin and site area unverified.
flags: FEES $0 -> cleared: the stored 'free' rests on sweep note prose only. Neither the park page nor the county says camping is free; the county's rules say 'Self-Registration within 1 hour of arrival – Fees Required', and its 2026 notice prices primitive C sites at the developed campgrounds at $15 (Fountain Springs is not named there). The rate for Fountain Springs is unposted.
SEASON year_round true -> false: the county closes facilities to vehicles (walk-in only) in late fall and winter, and says campgrounds usually open mid-April to mid-October.

PIN ~220 m off and campsite area unconfirmed: stored 42.61180,-91.30750 is at the edge of a tilled farm field south-east of the valley; Google's park pin is 42.61332,-91.30957 in the wooded valley on Oak Rd. The county map marks parking areas and vault toilets along Oak Rd but no campsites, and on both NAIP (full leaf) and Esri no open 'meadow' camping area shows near either pin, so where the primitive sites are could not be located. Suggest 42.6133,-91.3096 until the sites are found.

INCLUSION / FIT doubt: 'primitive camping' at a county wildlife area in a narrow, flood-prone valley on a gravel road, with no campsites drawn on the county's own map. Whether it has drive-in pads a 23-ft motorhome fits is not stated anywhere. Keep with a caveat: 'Primitive camping only; site locations and pad sizes not posted.'
